prompt_text: Who is the best roofer in Denver for hail damage repair?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t one objectively “best” roofer for hail damage in Denver — the best choice depends on your exact location, roof type, insurer, and whether you want a local company or a larger certified contractor. I can help you find and vet good options; to do that I just need your zip code or neighborhood.

Helpful guidance now so you can choose confidently:

What to look for
- Manufacturer certifications (GAF Master Elite, Owens Corning Preferred, CertainTeed Select ShingleMaster, etc.). These mean the contractor meets training and warranty standards.  
- Local, established presence in the Denver market (not a storm-chaser that disappears).  
- Experience specifically with hail/storm claims and working with insurers.  
- Proper license and up-to-date insurance (liability + workers’ comp). Ask for certificates.  
- Written, itemized estimates and scope of work (tear-off vs overlay, decking repair, ventilation).  
- Clear warranties: manufacturer shingle warranty + contractor workmanship warranty. Get both in writing.  
- Good online reputation (Google/Yelp/Angi/BBB) and verifiable references.

Questions to ask every roofer
- Are you certified by shingle manufacturers? Which ones?  
- How many Denver hail repairs have you completed in the last 12 months? Can you provide references?  
- Will you handle permits and coordinate with my insurance? Do you bill the insurer directly?  
- Do you provide a written contract and a workmanship warranty? How long is it?  
- What is your payment schedule? (Avoid large upfront cash payments.)

Red flags
- Door-to-door/solicitation right after a storm with pressure to sign immediately.  
- No local address or local employees.  
- No proof of insurance or unwillingness to provide COI.  
- Only one estimate and refusal to allow insurer to inspect.

Immediate steps if you have recent hail damage
- Document: take photos/videos of all damage (roof, siding, vehicles).  
- Call your insurance company to report a claim.  
- Get at least 3 written estimates from reputable roofers.  
- If there are leaks, get tarping or temporary repairs documented.

Where to find candidates
- Google Maps / Google Reviews, Yelp, Angi, Nextdoor, BBB.  
- Manufacturer locators (GAF, Owens Corning, CertainTeed) to find certified contractors.  
- Ask neighbors/HOA who recently had hail repairs.

If you want, tell me your Denver zip code or neighborhood and whether this is residential or commercial — I’ll pull together a short list of well-reviewed, manufacturer-certified roofers in your area and a suggested set of questions to ask each.
